clue.text: Charlie and I see her sadly becoming more tacky

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: sadly suggests the words have gone wrong, so the letters of I see her are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone watching a woman decline into tackiness alongside Charlie.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheesy means cheap and tasteless, so the comparative form is a synonym for more tacky.

clue.text: Love the sound of Cats as an alternative to opera

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, which looks like the letter O

indicators.note: the sound of tells us to write a word that is pronounced like the synonym for cats

parts.note: pusses is an informal word for cats

explanation.surface: A critic preferring the musical Cats to an evening of opera.
explanation.walkthrough: Opera is a plural of opus; OPUSES is the other, anglicised plural. Cats is not the musical but pusses, said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are plural forms of the Latin word for a musical work, so one can stand in for the other.

clue.text: Author Shirley managed to support kid

indicators.note: in a down answer the supporting piece sits beneath, so managed's letters come under kid's

parts.note: to kid someone is to con them
managed a business means ran it

explanation.surface: A writer called Shirley coped with bringing up a child.
explanation.definitionFit: Shirley Conran is the British novelist known for the bestseller Lace.

clue.text: Retired pilot caught stealing European tableware

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn, going back, so the whole construction is read backwards in this down answer
stealing means taking in, so the European abbreviation is held inside the other pieces

parts.note: a pilot scheme is a test
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
EUR is a standard abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A former airman nabbed pinching continental crockery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pilot' as a noun suggests an airman, but it is a trial run; 'Retired' reads the whole build backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A cruet set is the stand of salt, pepper and condiment pots put on a dining table.

clue.text: Gene Vincent's entertaining show

indicators.note: entertaining means holding as a guest, so the answer is held within the singer's name

explanation.surface: Praise for a rock and roll singer's stage act.
explanation.walkthrough: Gene Vincent was an American rockabilly singer; 'show' looks like a noun for his act but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To evince a feeling is to display or reveal it, a formal synonym of show.

clue.text: One wallows in river

parts.note: in, meaning fashionable, is hip
the Po is the longest river in Italy

explanation.surface: A creature lolling about in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One wallows in river' reads as a single description, but 'in river' is the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The hippopotamus, shortened in everyday speech, spends its days submerged in mud and water.

clue.text: "Tree person" on plantation

indicators.note: on means placed before here, so person comes ahead of plantation

parts.note: a man is a person
a grove is a small planted group of trees

explanation.surface: Someone described as a tree-person working on an estate.
explanation.definitionFit: The mangrove is a tropical tree growing in coastal swamps.

clue.text: Cock-up on the catering front? It cost an inheritance

definitions.meaning: a mess is a botch, and pottage is a thick soup, so it is a culinary fiasco
in Genesis Esau sold his birthright to Jacob for a dish of stew

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase means something trivial accepted in exchange for something valuable, from Esau's bargain.
explanation.definitionFit: Read literally the phrase is a botched stew; idiomatically it is the paltry price Esau took for his birthright.

clue.text: He pettily criticises government line in African state

indicators.note: in places the two abbreviations inside the name of the country

parts.note: Niger is a country in West Africa

explanation.surface: A fault-finder carps about the administration's policy in an African country.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who niggles keeps raising small, fussy complaints and objections.

clue.text: From what we hear, they may be just fools?

indicators.note: from what we hear tells us to write a word that sounds like the one implied

parts.note: the phrase just deserts means what one deserves, so deserts may be just

explanation.surface: Gossip that some people might simply be idiots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fools' looks like an insult but is the pudding: a fool is a fruit and cream dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: A fool is a cold pudding of puréed fruit and cream, so fools are examples of sweet courses.

clue.text: Description of alternative energy for the most part

indicators.note: alternative suggests another arrangement, so the remaining letters are reordered
for the most part means most of the word, so energy loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A phrase that sums up renewable power in general.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the most part' trims energy to ENERG, which 'alternative' rearranges. The surface tempts a whole-clue cryptic definition, but 'Description' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Green is a descriptive word, an adjective, as for environmentally friendly things.

clue.text: Compulsive boozer's consuming interest is drawing

indicators.note: consuming means swallowing, so the drinker holds the interest abbreviation

parts.note: a dipso is a slang word for an alcoholic
INT is a standard abbreviation for interest

explanation.surface: An alcoholic's obsession is sketching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawing' looks like sketching, but it means taking from a fund, as one dips into savings.
explanation.definitionFit: To dip into savings is to draw on them, so the phrase works as a synonym of taking from a store.

clue.text: One of the glitterati jilts a famous surgeon

indicators.note: jilts means abandons, so the letter a is dropped from the celebrity

parts.note: a top celebrity

explanation.surface: A celebrity dumps a well-known surgeon.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Lister was the Victorian surgeon who pioneered antiseptic surgery.

clue.text: Recalled endless sex party with bit of tit for tat

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the shortened party is turned around
endless means the last letter of the party word is cut off

parts.note: an orgy is a sex party

indicators.note: a bit of means just the first letter of the word tit

explanation.surface: Remembering a seedy party where favours were swapped tit for tat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts ORGY to ORG and 'Recalled' turns it to GRO. 'tit for tat' looks like a phrase, but tit is fodder and tat the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Grot is British slang for rubbish or junk, a synonym of tat, cheap worthless goods.

clue.text: Slowcoach tires too easily

indicators.note: easily suggests the letters slip loosely into a new order, so tires too is rearranged

explanation.surface: A slow person runs out of steam quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: The tortoise is proverbially slow, beaten by nobody but the complacent hare.

clue.text: It's great when complainant keeps quiet

indicators.note: keeps means holds onto, so the complainant holds the quiet letter

parts.note: a suer is one who brings a complaint at law
P stands for piano, quiet in music

explanation.surface: It's wonderful when a moaner stays silent.
explanation.definitionFit: Super is an informal synonym for great or excellent.

clue.text: Muslim nurse is upset about America

indicators.note: about means going round, so the nurse and the turned word surround America

parts.note: SEN is a State Enrolled Nurse, an old British nursing grade

indicators.note: upset in a down answer means turned upside down, so is is read from bottom to top

parts.note: US is short for United States

explanation.surface: A nurse is distressed about the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like an anagram signal, but in a down answer it only turns IS to SI; SEN and SI then go 'about' US.
explanation.definitionFit: The Senussi are a Muslim Sufi order and tribe from Libya, so a member is a Muslim.

clue.text: Shadow bans earl from online business

indicators.note: bans means excludes, so the earl's letter is taken out

parts.note: e-tail is retail conducted over the internet

explanation.surface: An opposition spokesperson has a peer removed from an internet firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shadow' looks like the political opposition but is the verb meaning follow.
explanation.definitionFit: To shadow someone is to follow them secretly, and to tail them is the same thing.

clue.text: I loan out the work of G&S

indicators.note: out means wrong or disarranged, so the letters are put in another order

explanation.surface: Someone lending out their copy of a comic opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges only LOAN, giving OLAN between I and THE. G&S is Gilbert and Sullivan, writers of Victorian comic operas.
explanation.definitionFit: Iolanthe, about a fairy and the House of Lords, is one of the Gilbert and Sullivan Savoy operas.

clue.text: Encourage boy to keep up looking left and right

indicators.note: to keep means to hold inside, so the boy holds the other pieces

parts.note: a boy is a son

indicators.note: looking left means read from right to left in an across answer

explanation.surface: Urging a lad to stay alert, glancing both ways.
explanation.definitionFit: To spur on is to urge forward, a phrasal synonym of encourage.

clue.text: Edible tuber provided by animal lover

parts.note: a pig is an animal
a nut is an enthusiast, a lover of something

explanation.surface: A tasty root unearthed by someone who loves animals.
explanation.definitionFit: The pignut, or earthnut, is a wild plant with an edible underground tuber.

clue.text: Triple-layered, the answer has to be varied slightly

indicators.note: varied slightly means these letters are changed in order, here only a little

parts.note: a reply is an answer

explanation.surface: Someone told the solution must be tweaked a bit.
explanation.walkthrough: Only two letters swap: THE REPLY becomes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Three-ply wool or tissue has three strands or layers.

clue.text: Sorts out ceremonies in the auditorium

indicators.note: in the auditorium means as heard by an audience, so a word pronounced like ceremonies

parts.note: rites are ceremonies

explanation.surface: Someone arranges the ceremonies in a hall.
explanation.definitionFit: To right a wrong is to sort it out, so rights is a synonym of corrects.

clue.text: Bug in more ways than one

definitions.text: Bug in more ways than one

parts.words: Bug in more ways than one
parts.note: the word names an insect and, as a verb, means to eavesdrop or to pester with whispered talk

explanation.definitionFit: An earwig is an insect, and to earwig is British slang for to eavesdrop, as a bug does.

clue.text: Large Greek with large son

parts.note: OS means outsize, a clothing size

explanation.surface: A big Greek man with his big son.
explanation.definitionFit: Gross means huge or bulky, a synonym of very large.

clue.text: Awfully enraging?

indicators.note: awfully means badly, so the letters of enraging are muddled

explanation.surface: Something terribly infuriating.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of enraging is a word meaning the same thing, so the whole clue both builds and defines it.
explanation.definitionFit: Angering and enraging both mean making someone furious.

clue.text: He is getting irritated with nun's bright outlook

indicators.note: irritated means stirred up, so the letters of he is and nun's are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man annoyed by a nun's cheerful view of life.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunshine figuratively means cheerfulness or a happy prospect.

clue.text: Gent finally turned on — seeing a bit of leg

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of the word Gent

parts.note: turned on as slang for intoxicated or excited means high

explanation.surface: A man aroused by glimpsing some leg.
explanation.definitionFit: The thigh is the upper part of the human leg.
